definitions.explanation: The internal framework of bones that supports and gives shape to the body of a human or animal.
The basic structure or framework of something abstract, such as an organization, plan, or argument.

examples.japanese: {人間|にんげん}の{骨格|こっかく}は{二百|にひゃく}{個以上|こいじょう}の{骨|ほね}からなる。
examples.english: The human skeleton consists of over 200 bones.

examples.japanese: {彼女|かのじょ}は{骨格|こっかく}がしっかりしている。
examples.english: She has a sturdy bone structure.

examples.japanese: {計画|けいかく}の{骨格|こっかく}を{決|き}めてから{詳細|しょうさい}を{詰|つ}める。
examples.english: We'll decide the framework of the plan before working out the details.

notes:
USAGE: {骨格|こっかく} is used both for the physical skeletal system and metaphorically for abstract frameworks or structures.

SENSE 1 COLLOCATIONS (physical):
・{骨格|こっかく}{標本|ひょうほん} (skeleton specimen)
・{骨格|こっかく}{筋|きん} (skeletal muscle)
・{骨格|こっかく}がしっかりしている (to have a solid build)
・{骨格|こっかく}{診断|しんだん} (bone structure analysis - for fashion)

SENSE 2 COLLOCATIONS (metaphorical):
・{計画|けいかく}の{骨格|こっかく} (the framework of a plan)
・{論文|ろんぶん}の{骨格|こっかく} (the structure of a thesis)
・{組織|そしき}の{骨格|こっかく} (the framework of an organization)

MODERN USAGE: {骨格|こっかく}{診断|しんだん} (skeletal/bone structure diagnosis) is popular in fashion consulting, where body type is analyzed to recommend suitable clothing styles.

RELATED:
・{骨|ほね} (bone)
・{骨組|ほねぐ}み (framework, skeleton)
・{骨子|こっし} (outline, gist)
